The decided functional scope of NoteDown, by area. This file describes the
current state of the concept: when a decision changes, the item is edited,
not appended to.

Each item says what NoteDown does (behavior terms) and, where it isn't
obvious, why. **Prototype** says whether the item is in `app/` yet
(round 1 = main view; round 2 = editor and dictation; round 3 =
multi-select; round 4 = sync and sharing; "app phase" = only possible in
the native app). **Open** names a question that blocks a decision. Items
without another source were decided with the user on 2026-10-13.

## Vision

NoteDown is a notes app in which every note is also a to-do: quick to
capture (typing or dictation), quick to tick off, and stored as plain
Markdown that stays readable in any other editor.

**Open** — who else it is for beyond the user's own use, and what sets it
apart from existing apps beyond the points above.

## Platforms

- **Android, iOS and web** are the target platforms of the app.
- The web app runs in desktop and mobile browsers, so all three device
  tiers in `PROJECT.md` → "Device tiers" stay in scope: phone and tablet
  through the native apps and the mobile web, desktop through the web app
  only.
- No native desktop apps (Windows, macOS, Linux) are planned; the desktop
  browser covers that use.
- **Open** — whether all three platforms ship at once; the technology is
  decided once function and look stand (`PROJECT.md` → "Technology
  direction").

## Functional areas

### Notes and storage

- Every note is one Markdown section, and every note is a to-do: it is
  either **open** or **closed**.
- Each note has a **created** date, a **last-edited** date and an optional
  **due date**; a closed note also keeps the date it was closed. Times
  are stored in UTC and shown in each device's local time; a due date is
  a calendar day (so devices and members of a shared file in different
  time zones agree).
- All notes, open and closed, are stored locally as Markdown: one file
  for the user's own notes, plus one per set of people notes are shared
  with ("Sync and sharing"); the metadata sits in an invisible comment per
  note so the files stay clean in other editors (`docs/file-format.md`). *Prototype: round 1
  (stored in browser storage, downloadable as `notes.md`).*
- Within a note, any Markdown is allowed, including further headings and
  task checkboxes; ticking a task checkbox doesn't close the note.
- An emptied note is deleted when editing ends, with Undo; a new note left
  empty is discarded silently. *Prototype: round 1.*
- **Local first:** every device keeps the complete notes on the device
  and works offline; in the app the files sit in the app's documents
  folder (visible in the Files app), in the web app in browser storage
  (`docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Where the files live"). *App phase.*

### Sync and sharing

Detailed in `docs/sync-and-sharing.md`; decided 2026-10-13, built in the
app phase.

- **Sync across devices** through NoteDown's own server, so notes written
  on the phone show up in the web app on the desktop. It runs
  automatically (after changes, on opening, on reconnect) with a status
  indicator.
- **End-to-end encrypted:** the server stores only encrypted files and
  never holds a key that decrypts them — notes are private by default,
  even from whoever runs the server.
- **Single notes can be shared** with other people. All notes shared with
  the same set of people live in one file for that set, encrypted so only
  its members can read it; sharing with one more person or removing one
  moves the note to the new set's file. All members are equal (edit,
  close, share further, remove, leave), and the whole note including its
  status is shared. Notes are shared with contacts; someone new gets an
  invitation link first.
- **Concurrent edits merge per note and per field;** when two devices
  changed the same text, both versions are kept (conflict copy) — nothing
  is lost. *Prototype: merge logic in `app/js/core/merge.js` (no live
  sync in the prototype).*
- **No accounts** (decided over email login: simpler, and keys come from
  the other person instead of the server): turning on sync creates an
  anonymous identity with a **recovery key** shown once. Devices are
  linked by scanning a QR code on the new device; **contacts** are added
  by scanning their QR code in person or by an invitation link. The
  server knows no names or emails. The app works fully without sync.
- The server is built to scale to many users (stateless API, database,
  object store).
- **Where it is operated** (decided 2026-10-13):
  - ⋮ → **"Sync & sharing…"** holds everything around sync: turning it on
    (name, then the recovery key, which has to be confirmed as stored),
    linking this device to an existing one (its QR code, or the recovery
    key), the devices (link a device by scanning, remove one) and the
    contacts (add by scanning or invitation link, show my code, remove).
  - **Sharing starts from multi-select** (long-press → Share), so one or
    several notes are shared at once; the share dialog lists the contacts
    with a checkbox each (a dash when only some of the selected notes are
    shared with that person), adds a contact on the spot, and offers
    **Leave** for notes of one shared file. Undo in the snackbar. Chosen
    over a toolbar or a per-card button: it follows the existing
    long-press pattern and keeps the cards calm.
  - **Shared notes show their members as initials avatars** in the meta
    line (up to three, then "+n"), one stable color per contact; tapping
    them opens the share dialog. Chosen over a colored stripe or a list
    grouped by people: it says who reads along and keeps one sorted list.
  - **Sync status** is a cloud icon in the top bar (synced, syncing,
    offline), hidden while sync is off; tapping it opens Sync & sharing.
  - Without sync, sharing explains that it needs sync and offers to turn
    it on. Notes in the archive aren't shared from there.
  - *Prototype: round 4, with a simulated server (`?sync=off` starts
    without sync, ⋮ → Go offline).*

### Main view and archive

- The **main view** shows the open notes; the **archive** shows the
  closed ones. Both look alike; the archive has a clearly different
  background tint. *Prototype: round 1.*
- A note is closed with its own round check button in front of its first
  line — distinct from the square task checkboxes inside the text. It
  moves to the archive, with "Note archived · Undo". *Prototype: round 1.*
- The **archive button** in the main view shows how many notes were closed
  today; the count resets at midnight. *Prototype: round 1.*
- Closed notes are **read-only**. In the archive, unchecking a note's
  round button reopens it (with Undo), and notes can be deleted
  (multi-select). *Prototype: reopen in round 1, delete in round 3.*
- The **+ button** sits at the bottom right of the main view. *Prototype:
  round 1.*
- Rendered notes show their **due date** as a chip: red when overdue,
  accent-colored when due today. In the archive the due date is shown
  without warning colors. *Prototype: round 1 (display only; setting it
  comes with the editor toolbar, round 2).*
- Reminders / notifications for due dates are not part of the scope yet
  (backlog #1).

### Sorting and search

- Both views sort by **last edited**, **created**, **due date** or
  **alphabetically** (first heading, else first sentence); the archive
  additionally by **closed** date. Each option can be reversed. Defaults:
  last edited, newest first; in the archive closed, newest first.
  Notes without the sort value (no due date) always come last. The choice
  is remembered per view. *Prototype: round 1.*
- A finished edit doesn't reorder the list right away, so a note never
  jumps away under the user's finger; the order updates on the next view
  change, sort or search. *Prototype: round 1.*
- A **full-text search** in the top bar filters the current view; the
  table of contents follows the filter. *Prototype: round 1.*

### Table of contents

- A table of contents over all notes of the current view, in the current
  sort order and search filter. *Prototype: round 1.*
- Levels count from the highest heading level that actually occurs; it
  starts with **2 levels** and **− / +** remove or add levels (between 1
  and the deepest level present). The level count is remembered.
- A note without a heading appears with its first sentence (shortened,
  italic) at the top level.
- Tapping an entry scrolls to that place in the note and briefly
  highlights the note.
- On the phone it opens as a **bottom sheet** from the top bar's contents
  button — within thumb reach, and the list stays visible above it
  (decided 2026-10-13 over a side drawer). Tablet and desktop show it as
  a fixed sidebar.

### Creating and editing

- A **new note** starts in edit mode with the cursor after `## `, ready
  for a level-2 heading; it stays at the top of the list until editing
  ends. *Prototype: round 1.*
- **Tapping into a note's text** starts editing it with the cursor where
  the user tapped, except on task checkboxes (they toggle) and links
  (they open). Closed notes don't enter edit mode. *Prototype: round 2.*
- The editor renders Markdown live like Obsidian's mobile app: only the
  lines the cursor or selection touch stay raw; headings, emphasis,
  inline code, links, quotes, bullets and task checkboxes are rendered
  on all other lines, and checkboxes can be ticked while editing.
  *Prototype: round 2.*
- Lists continue on Enter (bullets, numbers, tasks as open tasks); Enter
  on an empty item ends the list. Bold / italic never wrap the list or
  heading marker. *Prototype: round 2.*
- The text is saved on every change. Editing ends with **Done**, `Esc`,
  or a tap anywhere outside the note and its toolbar; the tapped target
  then acts normally (e.g. starts editing that note). *Prototype: round 2.*
- A **toolbar** helps with typical actions (as in Obsidian): heading
  (cycles ## → ### → #### → none), bullet list, task checkbox, outdent /
  indent, bold, italic, link, **due date** (today, tomorrow, in a week,
  pick a date, remove), a **microphone** that dictates at the cursor,
  undo / redo, and Done. On phone and tablet it sits above the on-screen
  keyboard and scrolls sideways; on the desktop it floats at the bottom
  of the list. *Prototype: round 2.*
- On the desktop the editor has shortcuts: Ctrl/Cmd+B bold, +I italic,
  +K link, +Enter tick / untick the task, Tab / Shift+Tab indent, Ctrl+Z
  / Ctrl+Shift+Z undo / redo. Outside the editor, `n` creates a note, `/`
  opens the search and `Esc` ends editing or closes a panel.
  *Prototype: round 2.*

### Dictation

- **Long-press on +** starts dictation into a new note, operated like
  Signal's voice messages: hold to record, release to save, slide left
  to cancel, slide up to lock for hands-free recording, then tap to
  finish. While recording, the + button shows a microphone, a bar shows
  the audio input level and the live transcript appears as a preview.
  The finished transcript becomes its own note (no heading — its first
  sentence serves as title), shown at the top with "Dictated note added
  · Undo". *Prototype: round 2.*
- The editor toolbar's microphone dictates at the cursor position: the
  not yet final words appear greyed at the cursor, final ones are
  inserted; tapping it again stops. *Prototype: round 2.*
- Speech is recognized in the device language. The prototype uses the
  browser's speech recognition (Chrome, Edge, Safari; needs https or
  localhost) and replays a sample transcript with `?dictation=demo`;
  the app uses the platform's recognizer (app phase).

### Multi-select

- **Long-press on a note** (450 ms) selects it and starts multi-select; a
  finger that moves first scrolls instead. Then a tap anywhere on a card
  adds it or removes it (task checkboxes, links and the round button
  don't act meanwhile). On the desktop, Ctrl+click starts / extends the
  selection and Shift+click selects a range. Long-press inside the note
  being edited stays text selection. *Prototype: round 3.*
- A selected note is marked only by the **accent border**; nothing else on
  the card changes (decided 2026-10-13 over a check in the round button
  and over a tinted card).
- While selecting, a **contextual top bar** replaces the normal one: ✕,
  "n selected" and the actions as icons (with labels on the desktop); the
  + button is hidden (decided 2026-10-13 over a bottom action bar: the
  thumb area and the list's bottom stay free, and search / archive can't
  be hit by accident). *Prototype: round 3.*
- Actions on the selection: **Close**, **Copy**, **Share** ("Sync and
  sharing"), **Merge** (two or more notes) and **Delete**. Close, Share
  and Delete end the selection and offer Undo. In the archive the actions are **Reopen**, Copy and Delete — no
  Merge, closed notes are read-only. *Prototype: round 3.*
- **Copy** puts the notes on the clipboard as plain Markdown, joined by a
  blank line, without metadata; it keeps the selection.
- **Merge** replaces the notes by one new open note: the bodies joined by
  a blank line, created = the earliest created date, due = the earliest
  due date, last edited = now. It appears at the top with "Notes merged ·
  Undo", which brings back the originals in place.
- Copy (with two or more notes) and Merge first show the notes in the
  current sort order in a **confirmation dialog**, where the order can be
  changed by dragging an entry's grip (arrow keys on the desktop); each
  entry is previewed by its first heading, or its first sentence if it
  has none. *Prototype: round 3.*
- Multi-select ends with ✕, `Esc`, the Android back button, when the last
  note is deselected, after Close / Delete / Merge, and on switching
  between main view and archive.

### Quick capture

- The app opens directly in the main view with the + button ready.
- **App shortcuts** "New note" and "Dictate" (Android: long-press on the
  app icon, iOS: Quick Actions). *App phase; not part of the web
  prototype.*
- A home-screen widget is not part of the scope yet (backlog #2).

### Look

- Themes from the **Catppuccin** palette: follows the system (light =
  Latte, dark = Mocha) by default; all four flavors (Latte, Frappé,
  Macchiato, Mocha) can be chosen. Accent color: Mauve. *Prototype:
  round 1, under ⋮.*
- App labels are English for now; a German translation can follow.
- Notes are shown as **separate cards** (decided 2026-10-13 over one
  continuous page): each note's boundary is clear for tapping into it and
  for long-press selection.

### Not in scope (for now)

Tags and folders / notebooks — until there is a concrete need.
